title: Lightweight Post-processing of Multi-model Subseasonal Rainfall Forecasts over India
question: Can lightweight, data-efficient post-processing improve multi-model subseasonal rainfall forecasts over India during JJAS?

season.name: JJAS initialization season
season.interpretation: Initialization dates fall in June--September; later lead windows may verify after September.

valid_date_alignment.weekly_statistic: arithmetic mean of seven complete daily rates

splits.split_unit: complete initialization with all six leads
splits.test_policy: no fitting, tuning, feature selection, normalization, calibration, retry selection, or threshold selection

truth.anomaly_rule: subtract the identical IMD climatology field from every forecast and observation
truth.support: stored IMD observation fraction multiplied by stored spherical India/region area

validation_weighted.formula: per-lead inverse validation RMSE, normalized to sum to one

features.piggycast_forecast_only: seven forecast anomalies plus six real ensemble-spread fields
features.piggycast_full: forecast-only features plus latitude, longitude, and sine/cosine of verification-midpoint day-of-year
features.location_calendar_only: latitude, longitude, and sine/cosine of verification-midpoint day-of-year

metrics.primary: case-level India-area-weighted spatial anomaly correlation, averaged over cases

uncertainty.method: paired circular moving-block bootstrap over ordered initialization dates
uncertainty.language: percentile effect intervals; no p-values or multiplicity-adjusted significance claims

neural_correction.role: complementary alternative; never sequentially applied after PiggyCast
neural_correction.current_status: excluded from common-date headline pending corrected +1...+7 retraining
neural_correction.reason: the existing independent-2025 control is frozen to +0...+6 valid-day windows
